results.title: Korea tightens corporate governance disclosure rules to strengthen shareholder protections
results.content: All companies listed on the benchmark KOSPI will face tougher disclosure requirements on boardroom changes and major corporate transactions under new rules designed to give shareholders greater oversight of corporate governance, financial authorities said Thursday. The changes, announced by the Financial Services Commission and the Korea Exchange, expand the information companies must provide in their annual corporate governance reports. The move comes after the reporting requirement was extended to all 826 KOSPI-listed companies this year. One focus is on preventing companies from circumventing the revised Commercial Act that is designed to give minority shareholders a greater say in board appointments. Under the law, listed companies with assets of at least 2 trillion won ($1.49 billion) must incorporate cumulative voting, which allows shareholders to pool their votes behind a particul

results.title: Most gov't agencies deny using VirusTotal, deepening questions over presidential data leak
results.content: Most government agencies told The Korea Times they do not use VirusTotal, the malware analysis platform where the personal information of the first couple was exposed for about five months, deepening questions over how the leak occurred. The paid platform had hosted sensitive personal information of 168 people aboard the presidential jet during President Lee Jae Myung’s trip to Europe in June. Those affected included not only the president and first lady but also high-ranking officials, including then-chief of staff for policy Kim Yong-beom, National Security Adviser Wi Sung-lac, current Prime Minister Han Seong-sook and several Cabinet members, as well as senior officials from Cheong Wa Dae and the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, security personnel and reporters traveling with the presidential delegation. results.title: US copyright lawsuit over BTS song 'Swim' dropped: report
results.content: American songwriters who earlier claimed that Korean superband BTS' chart-topping song "Swim" was copied from their own demo have withdrawn their claims in a U.S. lawsuit, a report showed Thursday. The attorneys for the accusers, who are three little-known songwriters, requested the judge to dismiss the lawsuit in its entirety in a court filing dated Wednesday (U.S. time), according to the Billboard. The move comes about four months after the songwriters — Steve Cooper, Jon Sandler and Greylyn Johnson — filed a lawsuit in July, claiming that "Swim" bears "substantial similarities" to their own song of the same name. The plaintiffs had named HYBE, HYBE America and BigHit Music as defendants, along with the song's credited writers, including former OneRepublic member Ryan Tedder. results.title: BCCK to hold special fundraising concert with John Walker
results.content: The British Chamber of Commerce in Korea (BCCK) and the Australian Chamber of Commerce in Korea (AustCham Korea) will jointly host a charity concert featuring John Walker and his band in Seoul on Friday to raise funds for people with disabilities and others in need. The concert will take place at Four Seasons Hotel Seoul’s bar OUL, starting at 6 p.m. Tickets are priced at 120,000 won and include admission, live entertainment, canapes and unlimited wine and beer. Additional donations can also be made before and during the concert. All proceeds from the event will be donated directly to the Myongdo Welfare Centre in Mokpo, South Jeolla Province. The center was founded and is managed by Sister Geraldine Ryan. results.title: SHINee's Minho gives up marathon record after pacemaker controversy, but fans rally behind him
results.content: SHINee member Minho has surrendered his marathon finishing time and apologized after footage showed a fellow runner apparently pushing him during a race. Yet rather than turning against the K-pop star, many fans are praising his response and predicting that his famously competitive spirit will drive him to return stronger. Minho completed his first full marathon at the 2026 JTBC Seoul Marathon, held at Sangam World Cup Park in Seoul on Sunday. He finished the 42.195-kilometer course in three hours and 18 seconds, narrowly missing the coveted "sub-three" milestone of completing a marathon in under three hours. Despite falling just 18 seconds short of his goal, Minho celebrated the experience and expressed his determination to try again. He also thanked a fellow runner who had helped him maintain his pace throughout the race. "I was able to achieve a good time thanks to Jun-hyung, who serv

results.title: Korea Eximbank backs Tanzania's AI ambitions with $170 million development loan
results.content: Korea will provide a $170 million development loan to Tanzania to build an artificial intelligence (AI) and digital technology training institute, marking the first AI-focused project financed through the country's official development assistance fund, the Export-Import Bank of Korea (Korea Eximbank) said Thursday. The loan agreement was signed the previous day in Tanzania's Dar es Salaam by Lee Dong-hoon, a senior executive director of the state-run lender, and Natu E. Mwamba, Tanzania's deputy finance minister. The project is the first under the government's so-called "K-AI Package," a development cooperation initiative that combines infrastructure financing with support for AI technology in developing countries. results.title: Hungarian calligraphers reinterpret Hangeul in new Seoul Exhibition
results.content: A Hungarian calligraphy collective has brought its unique interpretations of Hangeul to Seoul, showcasing Korean lettering through a European artistic lens. Munbangsawu, a Hungarian calligraphy group formed by students of the Korean Cultural Center in Hungary, has been invited to participate in the 2026 Asian Calligraphy Festival VI, which opens Thursday at the Seoul Calligraphy Museum inside Seoul Arts Center. The exhibition runs through Nov. 14 and features 15 works by 12 Hungarian members, making Munbangsawu the only invited foreign group from outside Asia. The members are also traveling to Korea to attend the opening ceremony, explain their works and introduce visitors to their experiences studying Hangeul calligraphy. results.title: Seoul turns public relations into viral comics, hitting 5.6 mil. views
results.content: Long known for its webtoon culture, Korea’s capital is transforming routine government announcements into emotionally driven digital comics — and its newest installment adds full animation and a soundtrack to connect with millions of readers. Seoul Metropolitan Government said Thursday that its first five policy webtoons have collectively recorded 5.67 million views and 80,000 comments, with each series surpassing 1 million views. The city released its sixth installment, “Seoul, 76 Years Later: Cadenza,” on KakaoPage at 10 a.m. Thursday, introducing its first moving webtoon, which combines animated sequences and background music with traditional comic panels. results.title: PM says sees no big change in alliance with US after Trump's election defeat
results.content: Prime Minister Han Seong-sook said Thursday she anticipates no big changes in relations with the United States after U.S. President Donald Trump's Republican Party suffered a crushing defeat in this week's midterm elections, adding the U.S. Democratic Party also considers the Korea-U.S. alliance important. "As both the Democratic and Republican parties have considered the alliance between the two countries important, I think there will not be very big changes in relations with Korea," Han said during a parliamentary budget committee meeting after a lawmaker asked her to assess the election results. She said the Democratic Party's victory was stronger than expected. results.title: Seoul Hanok Week draws 85,000, up 15% from last year
results.content: This year’s Seoul Hanok Week drew approximately 85,000 visitors — a 15 percent increase from 2025 — highlighting the growing appeal of traditional Korean houses as everyday cultural spaces, the Seoul Metropolitan Government said Thursday. Turnout for the annual festival has grown steadily, from about 35,000 in 2024 to 74,000 last year. The fourth edition of the festival ran for 10 days, from Oct. 2 to 11, in Bukchon, Seochon and other hanok neighborhoods across the capital. This year's theme was hanok in daily life. Some 180 participants, including the Swiss Embassy in Korea, local resident guides and artists, ran a record 82 programs, up 16 from last year. This year the city put more weight on hands-on programs than on sightseeing. A new exhibition drew about 17,000 visitors to six public hanok in Bukchon and Seochon that had been furnished with modern furniture and household items. Abo

results.title: 3 in 4 Seoul residents drink tap water: survey
results.content: Three in four Seoul residents now drink the city’s tap water, which is sold under the brand name Arisu, and more of them are drinking it away from home, a city survey showed Thursday. In the Seoul Metropolitan Government’s annual survey, 75.5 percent of residents said they drank tap water this year. That was up from 75 percent last year and 69.6 percent in 2024, when the city started using its own measure. The figure adds the 53.9 percent who drink tap water at home to the 21.6 percent who drink it only outside the home. The city created the measure because standards for calculating tap water drinking rates vary by country and institution. Under the American Water Works Association’s criteria, Seoul’s rate was 78.2 percent, 13.2 percentage points above the U.S. figure of 65 percent in 2024. results.title: Multicultural marriages in Korea edge down in 2025
results.content: The number of multicultural marriages in Korea edged down in 2025 from a year earlier, data showed Thursday, taking up 8.9 percent of all marriages. The country recorded 21,399 multicultural marriages last year, down 0.2 percent, or 51, from 21,450 in 2024, according to data from the Ministry of Data and Statistics. Marriages involving foreign wives accounted for 71.4 percent of multicultural marriages, followed by those with foreign husbands at 18.9 percent and those with naturalized citizens at 9.7 percent. The average age for first marriages was 37.1 years for husbands and 29.7 years for wives. Husbands were older than their wives in 75.2 percent of multicultural marriages. In 36.1 percent of all multicultural marriages, the husband was at least 10 years older than his wife. results.title: Foreign ministry fails to take steps even after learning of job scam crimes in Cambodia: audit agency
results.content: The foreign ministry failed to raise the travel alert for Cambodia or take other necessary measures in a timely manner, even though it had been aware that job scams targeting South Koreans were worsening in the Southeast Asian nation, the state audit agency said Thursday. Such crimes sparked public outrage last year after a South Korean college student was tortured to death by a Chinese scam ring in Cambodia, shedding light on a series of similar cases where young South Koreans were lured into the country with promises of high-paying jobs only to end up being kidnapped. According to the Board of Audit and Inspection (BAI), the foreign ministry learned after December 2023 through information from overseas diplomatic missions and private firms that South Koreans were falling victim to job scams and kidnapping in Cambodia, with the nature of the crimes becoming increasingly brutal. results.title: BOK chief to attend BIS governors' meeting in Switzerland
results.content: Bank of Korea (BOK) Gov. Shin Hyun-song will depart for the Swiss city of Basel this week to attend meetings with central bank governors from member nations of the Bank for International Settlements (BIS), his office said Thursday. During his six-day visit starting Friday, Shin is scheduled to join fellow central bank chiefs from BIS members in discussions on recent developments in the global economy and financial markets through the Global Economy Meeting, the Meeting of Governors from Major Emerging Market Economies and the Meeting of Governors, according to the BOK. He will also attend meetings of the BIS Board of Directors and the Economic Consultative Committee as a BIS board member. Shin previously served as head of the monetary and economic department at the BIS before being appointed governor of the South Korean central bank by President Lee Jae Myung in March.

results.title: Korean, Chinese filmmakers seek common ground beyond politics through AI
results.content: Despite political tensions and historical differences between their countries, two filmmakers from Korea and China believe stories of ordinary people helping one another can offer a path toward greater understanding. The directors, who won the top prizes at the China-Korea Artificial Intelligence (AI) Video Competition, drew inspiration from little-known acts of solidarity between Koreans and Chinese, using AI-generated films to bring those stories to life. The Chinese Embassy in Seoul hosted an AI short film competition, inviting young people from both countries to use AI to create videos highlighting stories of cultural exchange and friendship. One grand prize winner was selected from each country, with each receiving 15,000 yuan (3.08 million won) and a round-trip airline ticket to a destination served by China Southern Airlines. results.title: Hanwha Aerospace breaks ground on Chunmoo missile plant in Poland
results.content: Hanwha Aerospace has started building a factory in Poland to make guided missiles for its Chunmoo multiple rocket launcher, the company said Thursday. The plant takes its defense partnership with Poland beyond exports and into local production. The Korean defense firm held a groundbreaking ceremony Wednesday in Gorzow Wielkopolski, western Poland, for a plant that will be run by Hanwha WB Advanced Systems, its joint venture with Polish defense company WB Group. It will be Hanwha Aerospace’s first guided missile production facility outside Korea. About 250 government and industry officials from both countries attended. The plant will sit on a site of about 1.16 million square meters and is set to be completed in 2028. results.title: Korea Square draws 26,000 visitors in Hong Kong with 2-day cultural festival
results.content: A two-day celebration of Korean culture has drawn approximately 26,000 visitors in Hong Kong, nearly tripling last year's attendance and bringing Korean companies, local creators and public institutions together under one roof. Korea Square 2026, organized by the Korean Cultural Center in Hong Kong, took place Saturday and Sunday at PMQ's Courtyard & Marketplace and QUBE performance venue, transforming the central Hong Kong cultural complex into a showcase for Korean food, beauty, music, entertainment and design. Now in its sixth year, the festival attracted roughly three times the 9,000 visitors recorded last year, reflecting growing local interest in Korean culture, according to the center. More than 50 Korean companies, Hong Kong-based brands, creators and public institutions participated, including Samsung, LG and mobile game developer Com2uS, alongside the Korea Tourism Organization

results.title: Hyundai, Kia win int'l certification for in-house chip development process
results.content: Hyundai Motor and Kia have received international certification for the process they use to develop their own automotive semiconductors, the companies said Thursday. The carmakers held a ceremony Wednesday at Pangyo Tech One, their office complex in Seongnam, Gyeonggi Province, a tech hub just south of Seoul, to receive the certification from TUV Rheinland, a German testing and certification company. It confirms that their chip development process and functional safety management system comply with an international standard based on the rules of the International Organization for Standardization (ISO). Functional safety refers to designing electronic systems so that a vehicle stays safe even when a component fails. results.title: Myeongdong shops turn trash disposal into unexpected act of hospitality for tourists
results.content: Tourists wandering through Myeongdong can now enjoy street food and drinks without worrying about where to throw away their trash, thanks to an unusual initiative that turns local vendors into volunteer waste collectors. The Seoul Metropolitan Government and the Seoul Tourism Organization have launched a promotional campaign encouraging visitors to hand empty drink cups and food packaging to participating street vendors, who will dispose of the waste on their behalf. A total of 346 street stalls in Myeongdong are taking part in the Clean Myeongdong campaign, which aims to improve tourist convenience while keeping one of Seoul's busiest shopping districts clean. The initiative grew out of complaints from visitors who struggled to find trash bins after buying food and beverages from street stalls. results.title: Nexen Tire expands winter lineup with new model optimized for ice
results.content: Nexen Tire is expanding its winter tire lineup with a new model designed specifically for icy roads, targeting drivers who face treacherous conditions during early-morning and nighttime travel. The company said Wednesday it had launched the Winguard ice3 in Korea, adding an ice-focused option to its existing winter tire offerings. The new tire has earned the Ice Grip marking, a certification awarded to products that meet braking performance standards on icy surfaces. It is designed to maintain flexibility and traction in low temperatures through a specialized rubber compound, while its wider tread profile increases contact with the road. The product is aimed particularly at motorists who frequently drive through areas prone to icy conditions or travel during hours when temperatures are low and roads are more likely to freeze. results.title: Lee welcomes East Timor President Horta's visit to Korea ahead of summit
results.content: President Lee Jae Myung on Thursday welcomed East Timorese President Jose Ramos-Horta's first visit to Korea, expressing hope for a stronger partnership between the two countries on the occasion of next year's 25th anniversary of diplomatic relations. Lee wrote the message on his X account, as Horta was scheduled to make an official visit to Korea from Thursday through Saturday, marking the first trip to Korea by an East Timorese leader since the two countries established diplomatic relations in 2002. Lee and Horta will hold a summit Friday to explore ways to enhance tangible cooperation in various fields, including diplomacy, security, intellectual property, climate change and human exchanges. "The Republic of Korea and the Democratic Republic of Timor-Leste have built a longstanding friendship founded on our shared values of peace and democracy," Lee said, referring to the two countrie

results.title: Korea, Singapore, New Zealand review progress in green trade pact talks
results.content: Korea, Singapore and New Zealand have discussed progress in negotiations and key outstanding issues related to their trilateral Green Economy Partnership Agreement (GEPA), the industry ministry said Thursday. Senior officials from the three countries held a videoconference ahead of the APEC Economic Leaders' Week, scheduled to begin next week in China, according to the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Resources. Through the agreement, Seoul seeks to work with the two partners to jointly address the challenges posed by trade-related climate measures (TrCMs), including the European Union's Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM), and help businesses maintain stable operations amid an increasingly volatile global trade environment, the ministry said. results.title: Hanwha Aerospace breaks ground on Chunmoo rocket plant in Poland
results.content: Hanwha Aerospace said Thursday it has broken ground on a guided rocket manufacturing plant in Poland as part of efforts to expand its defense production capabilities in Europe. The Korean defense company held a groundbreaking ceremony Wednesday (local time) in Gorzow Wielkopolski, western Poland, alongside Hanwha WB Advanced Systems (HWBAS), its joint venture with Poland's WB Group. The plant, scheduled for completion in 2028, will mark Hanwha Aerospace's first guided weapons production facility in Europe. The facility will manufacture CGR-080 guided rockets for the HOMAR-K, the Polish version of Hanwha's Chunmoo multiple rocket launcher system (MLRS). The company plans to roll out the first batch in late 2029 before beginning full-scale production in 2030. results.title: Korea's stock markets to open 1 hour later Nov. 19
results.content: Korea's stock markets will start trading an hour later than usual on Nov. 19 due to the nationwide college entrance exam, the bourse operator said Thursday. Trading on the main KOSPI and secondary KOSDAQ stock markets will begin at 10 a.m. and close at 4:30 p.m., the Korea Exchange (KRX) said in a statement. On Nov. 19, an after-market trading session will also begin at 5 p.m., an hour later than usual, and close at 8 p.m., the KRX said. More than 551,000 high school seniors and graduates will take the one-day standardized College Scholastic Ability Test, according to the education ministry.

results.title: LG Twins sign ex-MLB pitcher Tristan Beck
results.content: The LG Twins announced their signing of former major league pitcher Tristan Beck on Thursday. The 2025 Korean Series champions said Beck, 30, agreed to a one-year deal worth $878,000, with $578,000 in salary and $300,000 in signing bonus. Beck was a fourth-round pick by the Atlanta Braves in the 2018 Major League Baseball (MLB) draft but was traded to the San Francisco Giants in 2019. He made his MLB debut with the Giants in 2023. In 85 outings, including five starts, for the Giants, Beck went 5-3 with five saves and a 4.08 ERA in 176 2/3 innings. He appeared in 14 games this year. The 30-year-old American also made 28 appearances in Triple-A this year, going 3-1 with a 4.54 ERA over 39 2/3 innings. results.title: Jung Woo-sung cast in upcoming Joseon-era action film
results.content: Actor Jung Woo-sung has been cast as a powerful politician of the Joseon Dynasty (1392-1910) in the upcoming Korean film "The Hit List," its production companies said Thursday. The film portrays cold-blooded politician Han Myeong-hoe (Jung), a key aide to King Sejo, who rises to power through his ruthless tactics but comes to face people seeking revenge after losing everything to him, according to Cheum Film and Studio Take. The film, which the production companies called "a hard-boiled, action-packed historical film," is based on a webtoon of the same name. Alongside Jung, its cast also includes actors Jung Sung-il, Baek Yun-shik, Wi Ha-joon and Choi Daniel. Kim Hong-seon, known for "Traffickers" (2012) and "Project Wolf Hunting" (2022), is the director. results.title: KRX activates sell-side sidecar for KOSPI on sharp fall
results.content: Korea's bourse operator on Thursday activated a sell-side sidecar for the benchmark Korea Composite Stock Price Index (KOSPI) as the stock index plunged. Program trading for the KOSPI-listed shares was suspended for five minutes at 10:16 a.m., according to the Korea Exchange (KRX). After opening 1.82 percent lower, the KOSPI surrendered 265.65 points, or 4.67 percent, to 5,418.15 as of 10:16 a.m. The index came under downward pressure following the Democratic Party's victory in the U.S. midterm elections, raising concerns over tighter regulations on artificial intelligence (AI) data centers. A sell-side sidecar is triggered when the KOSPI 200 Futures Index falls 5 percent or more for at least one minute.

results.title: S. Korea rejects Russia's criticism of joint military exercises with US
results.content: South Korea on Thursday rejected Russia's criticism of its joint military exercises with the United States, stressing that the drills are defensive in nature and aimed at promoting peace and stability on the Korean Peninsula. Seoul's foreign ministry issued the statement after a spokesperson at Russia's foreign ministry claimed Tuesday the South Korea-U.S. exercises are designed "to rehearse preemptive strikes" against North Korea, including with nuclear weapons, and urged Seoul "to respect Pyongyang's sovereign right" to ensure its own security. "The joint South Korea-U.S. military exercises are defensive in nature and are conducted annually to maintain a robust combined defense posture in response to North Korea's advancing nuclear and missile threats," Seoul's foreign ministry said in a statement sent to Yonhap News Agency. results.title: Shin Min-a, Lee Jin-uk to appear in upcoming romance drama
results.content: Actors Shin Min-a and Lee Jin-uk will portray a couple who reunite after a breakup in an upcoming romance drama set to premiere in the first half of next year, its broadcaster said Thursday. Set in a restaurant that only opens Wednesdays, Thursdays and Fridays, the series follows the love, forgiveness and growth of its lead characters, according to MBC. The Korean title of the series is "Wednesdays, Thursdays, Fridays." Shin portrays Eun-soo, who reunites with a boyfriend she broke up with 12 years ago, while Lee appears as the chef of the restaurant and Eun-soo's former boyfriend. The series also features Teo Yoo as Eun-soo's husband, a business executive. Joo Hyun, known for "The World of the Married," based on the BBC series "Doctor Foster," penned the upcoming drama, while director Jung Dong-yoon of the sports drama "Stove League" helmed the series.
